subject: BYOK/KMS exception + retention clarifications for VelociTech
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@velocitech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: BYOK exception + retention windows

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. VelociTech's security team reviewed the onboarding checklist and has two blocking items for our procurement: a BYOK exception request (their deploy will require our key material to remain in their KMS until go‑live) and clarification on default audit log retention for customer-managed projects.

Short asks:
- Can Redwood issue a temporary BYOK exception that allows us to bring our own key for the initial 30 days while we complete HSM provisioning? If so, what controls/logging do you require on your end?
- What is the retention period for request/audit logs tied to a private deployment by default, and can that be shortened to 90 days for regulated workloads?

I've attached a blank exception form from procurement and a suggested retention table.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can move forward with approvals.

— Jenna
Procurement | VelociTech
attachments: velo-byo-exception-form.pdf (pdf), retention-request.csv (csv)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: VelociTech Security <security@velocitech.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@velocitech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK exception + retention windows

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear summary and the forms. Looping in Karthik and Rishi to confirm technical constraints; copying Kimberly for commercial/contract implications.

High level response: we can consider a time‑boxed BYOK exception for an initial onboarding period BUT it requires explicit controls on key usage, scope-limited access, and additional audit traceability on our side. Karthik, can you confirm the minimum telemetry and logs we must capture if we temporarily accept customer-managed keys? Also: is 30 days feasible operationally or do we need longer?

I'll draft the contract language we normally use for this and share a working doc.

— Ava
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-byo-exception-form.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T13:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK exception + retention windows

Ava / team — quick technical note after a runbook review:

1) BYOK exception (temporary):
- Feasible if VelociTech provides a scoped KMS key with explicit allowlist for the Redwood runtime identity. We must ensure we never store plaintext key material; only the provider's KMS handles encryption ops.
- Required telemetry: key usage events (encrypt/decrypt requests mapped to request ids), initiation/teardown events for key bindings, and signed confirmation of key rotation policy while on exception. These must flow into our audit stream.
- Operational window: 30 days is tight. Recommend 45–60 days to allow for HSM provisioning and testing. 30 days would only work if VelociTech confirms HSM timeline and agrees to an expedited onboarding checklist.

2) Audit log retention for private deployments:
- Default retention: 365 days for compute/serving audit logs in private deployments (this mirrors our standard enterprise retention).
- Shortening to 90 days is possible but requires: documented business justification, adjustment to the retention pipeline (we can set a shorter retention policy per customer), and a signed waiver that elects out of our standard longer retention plus acknowledgment of implications for incident forensics.

I'll sketch the minimal telemetry fields we need and share as a CSV.

— Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Security & Runtime
attachments: telemetry-minimal-fields.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-19T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK exception + retention windows

Adding a few risk/ops items from Security Ops POV: 
- If we accept a temporary BYOK exception we need:
  * Daily integrity checks of the bind between the customer KMS and runtime (report to SOC team),
  * A dedicated retention bucket for the exception telemetry (so we can enforce the short TTL once exception ends),
  * A rollback playbook if we detect mis‑configured key permissions.
- For retention shortening (90d): require a one‑time technical review and a signed acknowledgement from customer that they accept reduced forensic history.

I'll volunteer to run the technical review with VelociTech's security lead.

— Rishi
Director, Security Operations

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@velocitech.com>, VelociTech Security <security@velocitech.com>
Date: 2027-01-19T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK exception + retention windows

Thanks — concise next steps for commercial/contract:
- We can offer a 60‑day BYOK exception window as a standard temporary approach. Will price as a professional services addendum to cover the additional operational overhead.
- If customer insists on 30 days, commercial will need an explicit SLA credit carveout and an expedited onboarding acceptance.
- For shortened retention (90d) we will accept with: signed waiver, SOC review completed, and price it as an options line item (to cover compliance tracking changes).

Ava — can you propose the contract language and I will run it by legal and finance? I'll also confirm pricing ranges and PS estimate.

— Kimberly
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@velocitech.com>, VelociTech Security <security@velocitech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-20T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK exception + retention windows — proposed path forward

Hi Jenna / security team — thanks for the patience. Summary and proposed path forward: 

1) BYOK exception: Redwood can grant a time‑boxed BYOK exception under the following conditions:
   - Window: 60 days (can consider 30 days only with explicit HSM provisioning schedule).
   - Controls: scoped KMS key with allowlist; no plaintext key material persisted; daily integrity checks reported to Redwood SOC; documented key rotation commitments.
   - Commercial: one‑time PS fee to cover onboarding and a short exception admin fee.

2) Retention: default is 365 days. We can set customer retention to 90 days for the serving/audit logs if VelociTech signs a waiver and completes the technical review with our Security Ops.

Action items:
- Jenna: confirm whether VelociTech can accept a 60‑day window and the proposed controls (reply by EOD Wed 2027‑01‑22).
- Karthik & Rishi: finalize the minimal telemetry CSV and run the technical review (Rishi to schedule call with VelociTech SOC).
- Ava: I will produce redlineable contract language and attach the PS estimate (draft attached).
- Marissa: please prepare a template PS SOW and pricing band we can reuse.

Attachments: redwood-byo-exception-form.pdf, proposed-retention-table.csv, PS-estimate-template.docx

Thanks all — want to get this to contract for signatures this week if VelociTech confirms.

— Ava
